title: Comparatives and Superlatives Quiz 3
description: Learn the irregular adjectives and the spelling changes.
instructions: Comparatives and Superlatives: Spelling and irregular forms.
Read each question carefully, then check your answer.
Every question has a trap. Read every word.

questions.question: Complete the table with the irregular forms.
questions.explanation: These adjectives do not follow the normal rules. Watch out: bad is worse, not badder.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: My cooking is badder than yours.
My cooking is worse than yours.
My cooking is worser than yours.
My cooking is more bad than yours.
questions.explanation: Bad has an irregular comparative: worse. Watch out: worser and badder do not exist.

questions.question: Double the last letter: hot, {{1}}; thin, {{2}}.
questions.explanation: After one vowel and one consonant, the consonant is doubled. Watch out: hoter and thiner are wrong.

questions.question: large, {{1}}; nice, {{2}}.
questions.explanation: Adjectives ending in e add only r. Watch out: not largeer.

questions.question: What is the comparative of 'happy'?
questions.explanation: Consonant + y becomes -ier. Watch out: the y is replaced by i.

questions.question: 'More better' is wrong because 'better' is already the comparative of 'good'.
questions.explanation: Better is a complete comparative. Watch out: never add more to it.

questions.question: What is the superlative of 'far' when talking about distance?
questions.explanation: Far has irregular forms: farther or further, the farthest or the furthest. Watch out: the most far is not used.

questions.question: Correct the mistake: This is the most easiest exercise.
questions.explanation: Easiest is already a superlative. Watch out: the double superlative is always wrong.

questions.question: Match each adjective with its comparative.
questions.explanation: These are irregular and must be learned. Watch out: many and much share more.

questions.question: Which spelling is correct?
questions.explanation: Hot has one vowel and one consonant, so the t is doubled. Watch out: do not triple the letter.

questions.question: Put the words in the correct order.
questions.explanation: Fast is short and takes -er, followed by than.

questions.question: Which pairs are correct?
questions.explanation: The first three are real forms. Watch out: much and good are irregular, so they take no -er.
